justification: Contribution is the DAG topology arranging 1000+ agents (MacNet) and the finding that irregular topologies win; evidence is lab benchmark runs, not deployment, so validation_research.
Headline artefact is OrchBench, a deterministic simulation instrument for scoring orchestration plans, not a loop mechanism; validated in the lab against Claude Code executions (r=0.816).
HieraMAS optimises intra-node LLM mixtures and inter-node communication topology, i.e. the arrangement itself; evidence is reasoning and coding benchmark runs in the lab.
The object is 12 collaboration topologies (authority, roles, dynamics) ranked against each other; a 2x2x2 factorial with 520 lab runs and automated evaluators is validation_research.
Compares four orchestration architectures (sequential, fan-out, supervisor-worker, reflexive) as the object of study; measured on a 10,000-filing SEC corpus in the lab, not in a live deployment.
DACS governs what context is held versus compressed per agent (registry summaries versus full focus injection); evidence is 200 synthetic trials against a flat-context baseline, all in the lab.
Proposes a RACI role-allocation framework across humans and agents, i.e. the arrangement of responsibilities; work-in-progress with one example implementation and validation only planned.
Claim is that orchestration-level LLM verification of result completeness gates and triggers replanning; evidence is 25 curated queries scored against a single-agent baseline in the lab.
RGAO's headline is a complexity-conditioned router selecting the orchestration topology plus a budget algebra; evidence is a lab prototype (misrouting 30.1% to 8.2%, DAG construction timing).
Studies how role configuration and team size govern collaboration, yielding role-design principles; 1,120 controlled trials over seven configurations in a lab FEA setting.
AMAS's dynamic graph designer picks a task-specific communication topology, so the contribution is the arrangement; validated on QA, math and code benchmarks in the lab.
Compares three architectural variants (FSM-aligned multi-agent, single-agent, unguided), so the object is orchestration structure; an eight-day RCT with 66 real users self-administering therapy.

The recipe targets the refinement step itself - error detection, critiquing unfaithful sentences, correcting - rather than agent arrangement; measured on three summarisation datasets and long-form QA.
AGAO allocates budgets and execution priority across an existing agent graph to suppress low-impact work, not to change topology; evaluated on multi-agent workloads against graph execution baselines.
Models inter-agent message dependencies as a propagation graph and governs what agents pass on via a message-layer plugin; evidence is seeded-error injection experiments over six frameworks.
OMAC optimises five MAS dimensions spanning agent functionality and collaboration structure, i.e. the arrangement; validated by lab experiments on code and reasoning tasks against recent methods.
The credited mechanism is iterative self-refinement cycles that correct the setup and design; demonstrated in depth on selected topology-optimisation problem classes, not in engineering practice.
HILA's headline is a metacognitive policy deciding when to solve autonomously versus defer to a human expert, a gate on unaided progress; evaluated on maths and problem-solving benchmarks.
BIGMAS contributes a graph topology designer plus a shared-workspace orchestrator routing among agents; validated on Game24, Six Fives and Tower of London against multi-agent baselines.
Systematically varies expertise-domain alignment, collaboration paradigm and system scale, so the object is the arrangement; a lab design study producing configuration guidelines.
AgentNet's claim is decentralised coordination with an evolving DAG topology and task routing without a central orchestrator; experimental comparison against centralised MAS in the lab.
Contribution is the DAG topology arranging 1000+ agents (MacNet) and the finding that irregular topologies win; evidence is lab benchmark runs, not deployment, so validation_research.
DynTaskMAS's core is a dynamic task-graph generator plus an asynchronous scheduler fixing execution order; evaluated in the lab by varying task complexity and agent concurrency.
Named limitation addressed is the absence of experience accumulation, fixed by an error-driven HER self-evolution loop rewriting prompts across episodes; measured on SWE-bench Verified and DevBench.
GroupDebate changes the debate arrangement - agents split into groups that share interim results - to cut tokens; validated by comparative experiments across multiple datasets in the lab.
